messages:
emma: Quick q — console quiet-mode granularity for SLO alerts. Right now UI only exposes tenant-wide quiet windows (1h/24h). Product wants per-route and per-SLO quieting so teams can silence a noisy endpoint without muting everything. Thoughts?

raj: strongly +1 to per-route. we see customers asking to mute a single noisy classifier while keeping other alerts live.

britt: per-slo makes sense, but beware complexity in the notify fanout logic. if a tenant mutes route A, do we still count toward error budget/telemetry? need clarity.

mike: reply to britt — we should still record the signals for telemetry and billing, but mark them as suppressed for notify. quiet-mode = suppress_notifications boolean + suppressed_reason tag.

sophia: UX note: in the console add a compact pill: "Quiet: route /api/v2/model (2h)" and link to inference details. avoid full modal for quick silences.

raj: dev-note: routing policy needs to map quiet requests to the Notify API. current API is /notify/suppress?tenant=...&window=24h — we need richer filters. proposal:

```json
POST /notify/suppress
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "scope": {"kind": "route", "route_id": "r-456"},
  "slo_id": "slo-789",       // optional
  "duration": "2h",
  "reason": "noisy third-party spikes",
  "suppress_actions": ["pager","slack-channel"],
  "record_signals": true
}
```

emma: that contract looks good. can we keep a backfill flag for retrospective suppression in telemetry so SREs can run queries excluding suppressed windows? maybe record_signals:false vs true.

britt: +1. also need to ensure quieting doesn't override per-route escalation policies (e.g., critical SLOs must still page). so maybe allow policy to set minimum urgency.

mike: implementation sketch — on suppress, Notify service emits a suppression event to the signal-ingest pipeline with metadata: scope, duration, id. Router checks suppression table before fanout. if slo.urgency >= CRITICAL -> respect minimum_urgency flag.

sophia: UI detail: add an "Always notify CRITICAL" toggle when creating quiet windows. default off, but enterprise tenants can set org-level policy.

raj: telemetry ask: create sample metric quiet.suppressed.count{tenant,route,slo} and quiet.suppressed.duration_bucket. will help show suppression coverage.

britt: think about race: if a suppression is created while an alert is mid-fanout, we still want deterministic behavior. maybe suppression has an "effective_at" timestamp and we only suppress requests with ts >= effective_at.

emma: good point. default effective_at = now + 0s, but UI can schedule for later.

raj: action items:
- raj -> PR for Notify API schema + docs
- mike -> router change to consult suppression table (canary on dedicated)
- britt -> update fanout runbook + ensure critical override path
- sophia -> console mockups for per-route & per-slo quiet pill
- emma -> telemetry proposal (metrics + dashboards)

mike: I'll add a lightweight acceptance test: create suppression, trigger alert, assert notify not sent, signals still persisted.

sophia: UX follow-up: add reason presets (maintenance, noisy-traffic, third-party). saves typing and helps metrics.

britt: 👍 also add audit logs for who created suppression (for compliance).

emma: thanks all — i'll open an umbrella RFC/PR with the contract and UX comps by EOD tomorrow. @raj please link any prior api-breaking concerns in the PR.
